report:
Fresh review of the complete callsite_updates claim, its one ordinary implementation entry (CompileTest::run in compile/mod.rs) and its one ordinary test (blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates). No TODO or N/A entry is present. Read the complete captured implementation file and test body plus captured blessing_gate design and the accepted RFD's ordinary-test/expectation-tooling rationale. No Rust edits, build or test execution in this review; the statements about test coverage describe inspected assertions, not a fresh test result.

Author-written locations and update destination: compile_test forwards each user expression directly into its field setter. observations, diagnostics and queries store the original expect_test::Expect values; neither the macro nor run constructs replacement expectations or temporary-file snapshots. run calls assert_eq on those same values only after preparation succeeds. Moving the Expect value through the builder preserves its callsite information. All three fields follow this identical storage/assertion mechanism. Temporary fixture files contain the evaluated Rust source, not recreated expectation macros. This realizes the RFD's decision to retain existing expect-test tooling and callsite literals.

The complete associated test exercises an actual downstream caller: it writes a disposable Cargo package with a visible compile_test invocation, an empty observation literal and an empty diagnostics literal. Its closure launches separate cargo test processes with the local harness dependency, pinned rustc, reused repository lock resolution and offline mode. The updating process explicitly sets UPDATE_EXPECT; each ordinary process removes it rather than inheriting the surrounding test environment. A stale ordinary run must fail with expect-test failure text and leave the caller source byte-for-byte unchanged. A successful updating run must write the rendered literal-22/u16 observation into that same caller source, retain the source annotation and the diagnostics expectation, and include exactly one rendered literal entry. This is direct evidence that the inline expectation is updated at the author-written location rather than only a temporary compiled fixture or the harness macro definition. Source inspection of unchanged Expect forwarding establishes why the macro implementation is not the destination.

Independent verification and ordinary immutability: after reading the blessed caller text, the test launches another independent non-updating cargo test process, requires success, and asserts the caller remains exactly equal to the blessed text. It therefore checks both ordinary mismatch/no-write behavior and ordinary success/no-write behavior, and does not mistake successful blessing alone for verification. The same test first introduces an unmarked rustc warning while updating, requires the compiler-marker failure and byte-for-byte unchanged source. That additional assertion supports the captured preparation boundary: only successfully prepared outputs can reach snapshot assertions. No claim that every snapshot field is separately integration-tested: the concrete update scenario covers observations and preservation of diagnostics, while inspection verifies common Expect handling for all fields. This coverage is adequate for the location/update-mode claim; no concrete defect or requested edit found.
